children: Russia's crude oil exports from its western ports are expected to fall to around 2.1 million barrels per day in September from about 2.2 million bpd in August as disruptions at the Black Sea port of Novorossiysk continue to curb shipments, two industry sources told Reuters.

Loadings at Novorossiysk are set to remain under pressure after collapsing in August following repeated Ukrainian drone attacks, which exacerbated a shortage of available tankers and increased loading delays, the sources said.

A sharp rise in attacks on vessels, ports and export terminals in the Black Sea has disrupted global oil supply chains, turning the region into another strategic chokepoint for international trade and limiting Moscow's export options.
On a daily basis, oil exports from Russia's western ports are set to fall 5% in September from August, the sources said.

Exports and transit volumes from Novorossiysk more than halved in August from July due to drone attacks, dropping from around 800,000 bpd to less than 350,000 bpd, according to Reuters calculations based on trader data.

The cost of chartering a Suezmax tanker, which can carry about 140,000 metric tons of crude, from Novorossiysk to India rose to around $20 million at the end of August, the highest level in several years, from roughly $13 million a month earlier. Many shipowners have become reluctant to send vessels to the port because of the heightened security risks.

One source said the September tanker schedule for Novorossiysk consists largely of cargoes carried over from the August programme, making it difficult to gauge the port's underlying export outlook for the month.

Planned crude loadings from Novorossiysk in September are expected to remain broadly unchanged from August levels, the sources said. A key uncertainty is the volume of Kazakh crude transit shipments that Russia is rerouting from the Baltic port of Ust-Luga to Novorossiysk.
Russia has been redirecting some Kazakh oil exports to Novorossiysk to free up capacity at Ust-Luga for additional Russian crude exports.

According to the sources, the scope for increasing crude shipments from Russia's Baltic ports in September is limited by terminal capacity constraints, while any further drone attacks could alter export volumes.
Ust-Luga came under a drone attack on Tuesday, although no damage to oil infrastructure was reported.
